to come, go

aorist infinitive of ἔμολον [I came] with future μολοῦμαι [I will come]. Of the former there are many examples in the tragedians, of the future one in Sophocles (OC 1742) and one in Aeschylus Pr. 689. The meaning of the verb is to come, to go, and it is used not only of persons, but also of things which happen either expected or unexpected.
Future μολοῦμαι [I will come]

An uncertain example is the spurious verse Sept. 613, where τείνουσι πομπὴν τὴν μακράν πάλιν μολεῖν [they stretch out the long procession to come back], but the copies have πόλιν [city], about which it has been said under μακρός.
